definition: A liquid state machine (LSM) is a type of reservoir computer that uses a spiking neural network.
details: An LSM consists of a large collection of units (called nodes, or neurons). Each node receives time varying input from external sources (the inputs) as well as from other nodes. Nodes are randomly connected to each other. The recurrent nature of the connections turns the time varying input into a spatio-temporal pattern of activations in the network nodes. The spatio-temporal patterns of activation are read out by linear discriminant units. The soup of recurrently connected nodes will end up computing a large variety of nonlinear functions on the input. Given a large enough variety of such nonlinear functions, it is theoretically possible to obtain linear combinations (using the read out units) to perform whatever mathematical operation is needed to perform a certain task, such as speech recognition or computer vision. The word liquid in the name comes from the analogy drawn to dropping a stone into a still body of water or other liquid. The falling stone will generate ripples in the liquid. The input (motion of the falling stone) has been converted into a spatio-temporal pattern of liquid displacement (ripples). LSMs have been put forward as a way to explain the operation of brains

explainer.lead: A liquid state machine enables computation over time-varying inputs without training a deep recurrent network. It matters because only a simple readout needs to be trained, simplifying learning for temporal tasks.

tiers.eli5: Imagine throwing pebbles into a pond: the ripples mix in complex ways, and you just watch a few spots to tell what was thrown. Here, the 'pond' is a randomly connected network, and you learn to read the ripples.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use an LSM as a fixed reservoir: they feed spiking inputs into a randomly connected network and train only the linear readout units. A pitfall is that the reservoir's dynamics must be well-tuned; too much recurrence and responses wash out, too little and they don't mix.
tiers.paperLevel: An LSM is a reservoir computer built from a spiking neural network: nodes receive external time-varying input and recurrent input from other randomly connected nodes, producing spatio-temporal activation patterns that linear discriminant units read out. Known limits include sensitivity to the reservoir's connectivity and the need for sufficient separation of input patterns.

explainer.example: A speech recognition task feeds audio-derived spike trains into an LSM, and a linear classifier trained on the resulting activation patterns labels phonemes.
